questions.q: What is a "module" in JavaScript, as described in this lesson?
options: A file whose exports other files can import
A special kind of variable that can only hold numbers
A single function that can never be reused
A blockchain-specific file type that only works with ethers.js
questions.explain: A module is simply a file that exposes exports for other files to import, enabling code to be split across files.

questions.q: How many default exports can a single file have?
options: Zero — default exports don't exist in JavaScript
Exactly two, one for each import style
Unlimited, same as named exports
Exactly one
questions.explain: A file can have any number of named exports, but at most one default export.

questions.q: What's different about importing a default export compared to a named export?
options: Importing a default doesn't use curly braces, and the importing file can name it anything it wants
A default export must always be imported using curly braces, same as a named export
Default exports are deprecated and no longer supported
Default exports cannot be classes, only plain functions
questions.explain: Since there's no exported name to match for a default export, the importing file is free to choose any local name.

questions.q: What is the key practical difference between CommonJS and ES modules, according to this lesson?
options: CommonJS only works in the browser, never in Node.js
ES modules cannot export more than one thing per file
There is no functional difference between the two systems
CommonJS (require/module.exports) loads synchronously at runtime, while ES modules (import/export) are parsed statically before the code runs
questions.explain: This runtime-vs-static-parsing distinction is the substantive difference between the two module systems.

questions.q: Given export function add(a, b) { return a + b; } in math-helpers.js, how would another file import it?
options: require("./math-helpers.js").default;
import add from "./math-helpers.js";
It cannot be imported since it's a function, not a class
import { add } from "./math-helpers.js";
questions.explain: Since add is a named export, importing it requires curly braces matching the exported name.
